items.statement: On every admitted finite input of [[alg-scaled-householder-reflector-formation-and-application]], the formation and application procedure terminates with its specified identity, reflector or first-failure return. Each specified separate-block application also terminates with its output or first failure. The zero-column branch returns the identity action and the copied block without evaluating a reflector denominator. In a successful nonzero-column branch the stored vector is nonzero, so its associated exact real reflector is orthogonal and also acts unitarily on complex blocks. This statement asserts neither unconditional arithmetic success nor a backward-error bound for a successful call.
items.strategy:
1.1 The zero test scans a finite column. If it succeeds, [F1] returns its initialized identity record, zero target and copied finite block without forming any squared-vector norm or quotient. Otherwise the scaling maximum, the two norm sums, coefficient formation, column dots and ordered update products each use finitely many indices. By [F2], each attempted arithmetic operation returns its next value or a first failure. The extra finite positivity and normality tests either return failure or allow the next finite stage. Thus formation and application terminate with a declared record. [given, F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 A specified separate block has finitely many columns and rows. Its sequential dots, coefficient-vector products and ordered update products have finite bounds; [F2] again makes each attempt return or fail. Hence this additional application terminates, including zero columns of the separate block. [given, F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 In a successful nonzero-column branch, the stored squared-norm sum is positive by [F1]. If the stored vector were zero, every square and every sum in that computation would be exact zero by [F2], contradicting that positive test. Therefore $v\ne0$ and $d=v^Tv>0$. For $K=vv^T/d$, direct multiplication gives $K^T=K$, $K^2=K$ and $(I-2K)^T(I-2K)=I$. Its real entries give the same adjoint identity over $\mathbb C$. Together with steps 1.1–1.2 this proves every stated status and representative property. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra] ∎

items.statement:
Let $R\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ be upper triangular with stored floating-point entries and nonzero diagonal, and let $y\in\mathbb R^n$ have stored floating-point entries, where $n\ge1$ and $(n+3)u<1$. Use the operationwise arithmetic model of [[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]] at unit roundoff $u$. Compute descending substitution by the sequential rounded dot $s_i=\operatorname{fl}(\sum_{j>i}R_{ij}\widehat x_j)$ (empty sum zero), $t_i=\operatorname{fl}(y_i-s_i)$, and $\widehat x_i=\operatorname{fl}(t_i/R_{ii})$. Assume each exact intermediate is zero or normal and each rounded result is finite, so every operation succeeds under that model. Then there is upper triangular $\Delta R$ with
$$(R+\Delta R)\widehat x=y,\qquad |\Delta R|\le\gamma_{n+3}|R|,\qquad \|\Delta R\|_F\le\gamma_{n+3}\|R\|_F.$$
In particular $\widehat x=0$ forces $y=0$. Forward substitution has the transposed conclusion.
items.strategy:
1.1 Expand the rounded dot to obtain $s_i=\sum_{j>i}R_{ij}\widehat x_j(1+\theta_{ij})$, with $|\theta_{ij}|\le\gamma_{n-i}$, and use $s_n=0$. Write subtraction and division errors as $\alpha_i,\beta_i\in[-u,u]$. The computed row identity is then $R_{ii}\widehat x_i/((1+\alpha_i)(1+\beta_i))+\sum_{j>i}R_{ij}\widehat x_j(1+\theta_{ij})=y_i$. These identities also hold for zero intermediates by taking the corresponding error zero. [given, F1, F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 Choose $\Delta R_{ii}=R_{ii}(((1+\alpha_i)(1+\beta_i))^{-1}-1)$ and $\Delta R_{ij}=R_{ij}\theta_{ij}$ for $j>i$, with zeros below the diagonal. Since $u<1/(n+3)\le1/4$, all denominators are positive and $|((1+\alpha_i)(1+\beta_i))^{-1}-1|\le(1-u)^{-2}-1\le3u/(1-3u)=\gamma_3$; multiplying positive denominators verifies the last inequality. Thus every entry has the claimed bound. [F1, step 1.1, algebra, construct]

3.1 Step 1.1 gives $(R+\Delta R)\widehat x=y$, and summing the squared entry bounds gives the Frobenius estimate. If $\widehat x=0$, the same equation gives $y=0$, including dimension one without a division by $\|\widehat x\|$. Reversing the row order proves the lower-triangular version. [step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

items.title: Rounded matrix products give certified linear and normal-equation residual allowances
items.statement:
Let $A\in\mathbb F^{m\times n}$, $x\in\mathbb F^n$, $y\in\mathbb F^m$ have stored real or complex entries, with $m,n\ge1$. Use the operationwise arithmetic model, successful sequential dot products, and $0<u<1$ with $(\max(m,n)-1)u<1$. Define
$$g_k=\frac{1+6u}{1-(k-1)u}-1,\qquad F=\|A\|_F,\quad X=\|x\|_2,\quad Y=\|y\|_2.$$
For $\widehat v=\operatorname{fl}(Ax)$ and $\widehat w=\operatorname{fl}(\widehat v-y)$, put $V=g_nFX$ and $W=V+u(\|\widehat v\|_2+Y)$. Then
$$\|\widehat w-(Ax-y)\|_2\le W.$$
For a stored real $\lambda>0$, also compute $\widehat z=\operatorname{fl}(A^*\widehat w)$, $\widehat l=\operatorname{fl}(\lambda x)$ and $\widehat r=\operatorname{fl}(\widehat z+\widehat l)$, rounding scalar multiplication componentwise. The exact intended normal residual $r=A^*(Ax-y)+\lambda x$ satisfies
$$\|\widehat r-r\|_2\le\rho:=FW+g_mF\|\widehat w\|_2+u\lambda X+u(\|\widehat z\|_2+\|\widehat l\|_2).$$
Norms in these certificates mean exact norms or certified upper bounds. Uncontrolled rounding of the certificate itself is not authorized. The linear bound applies columnwise to certify $\|I-AB\|_2\le\|I-AB\|_F$ from stored basis-solve columns $B$.
items.strategy:
1.1 For $(a+ib)(c+id)$, each rounded real product has error at most $u$ times its absolute exact value. Each final real addition contributes at most $u(1+u)$ times the two corresponding product magnitudes. The Euclidean norm of the resulting real/imaginary error is at most $2(2u+u^2)|a+ib||c+id|\le6u|a+ib||c+id|$, since $u<1$. Conjugation is exact. Real products obey this conservative bound as well. [given, F1, algebra]

2.1 In a length-$k$ dot product, each product error from step 1.1 is propagated through at most $k-1$ additions. Expansion of each real component and [F2] bound the dot discrepancy by $[6u+\gamma_{k-1}(1+6u)]\sum_i|a_i||x_i|=g_k\sum_i|a_i||x_i|$, with $\gamma_0=0$. Combining rows and applying Cauchy-Schwarz gives $\|\widehat v-Ax\|_2\le g_nFX=V$. Componentwise subtraction has vector error at most $u(\|\widehat v\|_2+Y)$, so the linear residual allowance is $W$. Zeros cause no difficulty in this expansion. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Apply step 2.1 to $A^*\widehat w$ to get $\|\widehat z-A^*\widehat w\|_2\le g_mF\|\widehat w\|_2$. Transporting the earlier error through $A^*$ adds at most $FW$. The scalar product error is at most $u\lambda X$; the last addition adds at most $u(\|\widehat z\|_2+\|\widehat l\|_2)$. Their sum proves $\rho$. For basis columns, the triangle inequality combines each computed linear residual with its allowance; summing the squared column bounds gives a Frobenius certificate for $I-AB$, which bounds its induced Euclidean norm by Cauchy-Schwarz. [F1, F3, step 2.1, algebra] ∎
